text:
carmen_support: FYI ACME reports 500s + very high p95 from EU users. They say requests are being served from us-east. Seeing auth/tenant-mismatch errors. Escalating.

marta_cs: They're on the phone now, started around 09:12 UTC after a config push.

carmen_support: Example from their support dump: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
x-served-region: us-east-1
x-error: auth/tenant-mismatch
trace-id: 01FZ...
```

ingrid_sre: I'm tailing the edge router logs. I see a pattern: when eu pool latency spikes we evaluate the fallback policy and select the 'primary' region (us-east) due to an inverted distance comparator. That causes tenant-scoped auth checks to fail (tenant bound to eu registry). Also retries cause duplicate token-metering. Repro plan: 
1) simulate eu-backend high RT
2) send 5 concurrent requests with `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1`
3) observe `x-served-region` header and intermittent 5xx

carmen_support: repro verified locally with a small curl loop — can attach logs.

raj_eng: I have a quick patch to fix comparator and add a guard to prefer header-pinned region when present. Pushing a canary to routers now. Also adding a fallback cap so we stop retrying to a different region more than twice.

eve_billing: Heads up — billing noticed increased token counts for the ACME org during the incident window (retries counted as usage). Opening a billing incident and preparing a temporary credit while we audit.

neil_oncall: Rolling routing rules back to the previous stable set (pre-09:12) while patch lands. Rollback started 09:48 UTC. Please confirm metrics.

ingrid_sre: After rollback p95 for eu clients dropped from ~620ms to ~95ms, error rate returned to baseline. Auth failures stopped by ~10:02 UTC.

marta_cs: ACME accepted an apology + temporary credit. They've requested a clear postmortem and timeline.

carmen_support: Support repro checklist for CS / oncall: 
```
1) curl with X-Client-Region header to reproduce
2) check `x-served-region` in response headers
3) include trace-id when escalating to #incidents and ops
```

raj_eng: PR #8424: fixes comparator, adds unit + integration tests for region flap scenarios, and adds header-pin precedence. Will merge after canary verification (10:20 UTC).

eve_billing: Affected org ids collected (internal doc link). We propose a 10% credit for ACME due to double-charging exposure; following up with full audit.

ingrid_sre: Draft postmortem notes: 
- Incident: region fallback selected wrong region causing auth/tenant-mismatch + elevated latency for EU traffic.
- Root cause: comparator in fallback policy treated larger distance as better (inverted logic).
- Contributing factors: insufficient integration tests for cross-region failover; retry billing logic counts short retries as billable tokens.
- Mitigation: rollback to stable routing rules; hotfix to comparator + header-pin precedence; billing credit and audit.
- Follow-ups: add chaos/region-flap tests to CI, update routing policy docs, change billing to flag/review quick routing retries (<1s) and not bill until final success.

neil_oncall: Assigning follow-ups: @raj_eng routing fix owner, @eve_billing billing remediation, @marta_cs customer comms, @ingrid_sre add chaos test. I'll move this to the postmortems channel and draft the official timeline. :thumbsup:

carmen_support: Thanks all — attaching customer logs and trace-ids to the postmortem thread.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of raj_eng/region-fix v2 started at 10:15 UTC -> health checks passing.

marta_cs: Customer happy with timeline + credit, asked for KB entry so CS can run quick checks next time. I'll draft it. :white_check_mark: 

ingrid_sre: Closing incident channel notes here. Will create follow-up tickets for chaos tests + billing guard rails.

neil_oncall: Closing thread — moving to incident archive.
